test_total does not fail. It passes. The failing test is test_half_cent_rounds_up.

Test run (python -m pytest -q test_cart.py): 1 failed, 2 passed.
  test_plain                 passed
  test_total                 passed  (399 * 0.9 = 359.1, int() gives 359, expected 359)
  test_half_cent_rounds_up   FAILED  assert 959 == 960

Why test_half_cent_rounds_up fails:
  total() computes int(subtotal * (1 - discount_percent / 100)).
  int() truncates toward zero, it does not round.
  1010 * 0.95 is 959.5 exactly in floating point, int() truncates it to 959.
  The test expects 960 (half cent rounds up).

So the cause is the truncation in cart.py, line 8: int(...) instead of a round-half-up.
Note: Python's round() rounds half to even (round(959.5) is 960 here, but round(958.5) would be 958),
so a round-half-up fix would need integer arithmetic, for example (subtotal * (100 - discount_percent) + 50) // 100.

Nothing was changed. No fix was built; the question was answered only.
Open: did you mean test_half_cent_rounds_up, or is there a different test_total elsewhere?
